req.title: Reject wrong method on /delete
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 for methods other than DELETE on /delete.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /delete must return HTTP 405 for any method other than DELETE. We need: (1) a positive test confirming DELETE returns 200, (2) negative tests confirming non-DELETE methods return exactly 405, and (3) boundary tests covering the full set of common HTTP methods. Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting exact status codes (405 vs 200), testing both sides of the method-allowed boundary, and covering multiple wrong-method variants to catch any operator or constant mutation in Flask's method routing.

expected: Response body is valid JSON with expected keys
trace: R-HTTPBIN-011: DELETE on /delete must succeed with 2xx
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_method_returns_200():
    r = client.delete('/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(data, dict)
    assert 'url' in data
    assert 'headers' in data
    assert 'args' in data

test_delete_method_returns_200()

tests.name: test_all_non_delete_methods_return_405
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, HEAD requests to /delete
trace: R-HTTPBIN-011: boundary between allowed (DELETE=200) and disallowed (all others=405)
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_all_non_delete_methods_return_405():
    wrong_methods = [
        ('GET', client.get),
        ('POST', client.post),
        ('PUT', client.put),
        ('PATCH', client.patch),
    ]
    for method_name, method_fn in wrong_methods:
        r = method_fn('/delete')
        assert r.status_code == 405, f"{method_name} expected 405, got {r.status_code}"
        assert r.status_code != 200, f"{method_name} must not return 200"
        assert r.status_code != 404, f"{method_name} must not return 404"
    r_delete = client.delete('/delete')
    assert r_delete.status_code == 200

test_all_non_delete_methods_return_405()

tests.name: test_delete_response_body_structure
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send DELETE request to /delete with a query parameter
Inspect response JSON body for expected keys
expected: JSON body contains keys: url, args, headers, origin
trace: R-HTTPBIN-011: positive path — DELETE returns 200 with correct payload structure
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_response_body_structure():
    r = client.delete('/delete?foo=bar')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data is not None
    for key in ('url', 'args', 'headers', 'origin'):
        assert key in data, f"Missing key: {key}"
    assert data['args'] == {'foo': 'bar'}

test_delete_response_body_structure()

def test_405_not_404_for_wrong_method():
    r = client.get('/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 405

    assert r.status_code != 400
    assert r.status_code != 403
